arithmetic_intensity.description: bytes moved per flop, and at what batch size

scales_with.description: knobs that change this cost: batch, context_length, hidden_width, num_experts, ...

values_for.description: bare accelerator ids, only where the record commits to named parts

magnitude.description: the figures the record itself quotes for this parameter, verbatim

basis.description: where the claimed effect comes from: recorded = the record cites a source or vendor/architecture statement for it; derived = it follows from the record's own arithmetic; unverified = asserted but not sourced at the part level. null = not established. NEVER fill this to make a row look better sourced than it is.

hardware_parameters.description: The hardware QUANTITIES that change this class's cost, as opposed to affected_by_hardware, which holds the PRODUCTS (accelerator record ids). Added 2026-10-05. WHY THIS FIELD EXISTS, and the failure it fixes: affected_by_hardware is a cross-reference field, so a wave-4 crawler put ['memory_bandwidth', 'l2_cache_size', 'tensor_core_count'] into it - hardware PARAMETERS, not products. They could never resolve, and worse they silently consumed the dangling-reference budget that exists to catch NEW bad references. A later pass removed them from that field and pushed them into free-text notes, which made them unqueryable prose; qhw-decode-gemm-memory-bound still carries the incident in its notes with affected_by_hardware left EMPTY, which is correct (it is part-independent) but loses the fact that bandwidth, L2 size and tensor-core count are the variables that SET the ridge point. This field is where a part-independent dependency belongs. A row here is a CLAIM that this parameter moves this class; it is not a measurement of any part, and `magnitude` carries the figures the record already quotes rather than a new number. NEVER invent a value here: if the effect is not sourced, set basis 'unverified' or leave the row out.

sources.description: source ids; each must exist in data/sources/
